title.rendered: The One Who Came Back: Thanks That Turns Around | The Thankful Heart, Day 3

excerpt.rendered: In Luke 17:15-19 ten lepers were healed, but only one returned to give thanks. Day 3 of The Thankful Heart turns us back to the feet of Jesus.

content.rendered:
Ten men were healed. Only one came back. The miracle happened to all ten, but only one turned around and found the Healer. Thanksgiving is how a blessing becomes a relationship.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, November 17, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 3

Today’s Scripture

“And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, returned, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at His feet, giving Him thanks. And he was a Samaritan. So Jesus answered and said, ‘Were there not ten cleansed? But where are the nine? Were there not any found who returned to give glory to God except this foreigner?’ And He said to him, ‘Arise, go your way. Your faith has made you well.’”
Luke 17:15-19 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Ten lepers stood at a distance and lifted up their voices, crying out to Jesus for mercy. He told them to go and show themselves to the priests, and as they went, they were cleansed. Imagine the moment. Skin that had been dead and white turning healthy as they walked. Ten lives given back on a single road.

Nine kept walking. We should not be too hard on them. They were doing exactly what Jesus had told them to do. They were heading for the priest, for their families, for the life they had lost. But one man stopped in the road. “When he saw that he was healed, returned.” He turned around. He raised his voice. He fell on his face at the feet of Jesus and gave Him thanks.

Luke adds a detail that would have startled his first readers: “And he was a Samaritan.” The outsider, the one least expected to know the right response, was the one who came back. Gratitude is not a matter of background or religious training. It is the response of a heart that has seen what has been done for it. Whether you grew up in church in Manila or met Jesus last month in Dubai, the way back to His feet is open to you.

Then listen to the final words Jesus spoke over him: “Arise, go your way. Your faith has made you well.” All ten were cleansed. But this one received something more: a face to face encounter with the One who healed him, and words of wholeness spoken over his whole life. The nine had their skin restored. The one had his heart restored to God.

Every one of us has received more than we can count in Christ. Forgiveness, new life, His Spirit, His nearness. The invitation today is simply to turn around. Stop in the road of your busy week and go back to His feet. Name what He has done, out loud if you can. Thanksgiving does not earn the blessing. It brings you face to face with the One who gave it.

How the Thankful Heart Returns

It notices what God has done. “When he saw that he was healed,” he turned back. Gratitude begins with seeing.

It goes back to the Person, not just the gift. He returned to the feet of Jesus, not to the miracle.

It receives the deeper word. Thanksgiving draws us close enough to hear Jesus say, “Your faith has made you well.”

Declaration

Lord Jesus, I thank You that You have cleansed me and made me whole (Luke 17:19). Like the one who came back, I turn around and come to Your feet with thanks. I thank You that Your blood has forgiven all my sins (Colossians 1:14) and that I who was far off have been brought near (Ephesians 2:13). I will not hurry past Your goodness. I see what You have done, and I give You glory with my whole voice. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
